fatal_errors: The proposed temperature of approximately 600 °C is incompatible with the immersed 25–100 °C tribo-corrosion study and changes the relevant oxidation, aqueous-corrosion, and film-formation physics.

The hypothesis assigns degradation to galvanic attack and cohesion loss at eutectic interphase boundaries, but no evidence for preferential interphase corrosion, phase-potential differences, or interface weakening is supplied.

The comparison of combined wear-corrosion with corrosion-only cannot establish synergistic acceleration because any extra loss may simply be direct mechanical wear; a wear-only condition and an additive wear-plus-corrosion reference are needed.
The hypothesis misses the observed nonmonotonic temperature response, with minimum degradation near 50 °C and increased tribo-layer disruption at 100 °C.

It omits the matched DS2205 comparator and reverses the central material-level conclusion that the HEA exhibits comparatively robust passivation and much lower wear rather than exceptional accelerated degradation.
explanation: The response recognizes the general depassivation–repassivation coupling inherent to tribo-corrosion and proposes a nominally controlled comparison, but it does not reconstruct the study. The actual mechanism involved competition among abrasion, thermally activated film repair, and tribo-layer fracture across 25, 50, and 100 °C, with a polishing/minimum-wear regime near 50 °C. The proposed 600 °C interphase-galvanic feedback is unsupported and outside the experimental domain. It also fails to predict separate wear and electrochemical responses relative to the identically conditioned DS2205 baseline. Its falsification test is not mechanism-specific: higher loss under sliding than under corrosion-only is expected from ordinary wear and would not demonstrate galvanic interphase attack. Spatially resolved electrochemical evidence, interphase-selective damage, wear-only controls, and comparison against the additive independent losses would be required. No supporting evidence is cited.
